newsitem.title: USA: Swiss bank housed looted Jewish paintings - documents.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bank housed looted Jewish paintings - documents.

text.p: The Union Bank of Switzerland, under fire for shredding Second World War documents, stored stolen paintings for the Nazis and was suspected by the Allies of providing them with large amounts of Swiss francs, according to U.S. government documents released on Thursday.

The documents were released by the World Jewish Congress as a debate raged in Switzerland over whether the bank's shredding of documents from a subsidiary contained information about accounts held by Jews before and during the war.

The bank said the hundreds of pounds of documents it shredded had no bearing on efforts to find dormant Jewish accounts or trace Swiss bank dealings with the Nazis, but no inventory was kept. A new Swiss law forbids banks to shred documents pertaining to bank dealings during the war.

The documents released by the WJC charged that Union Bank, one of Switzerland's biggest banks, stored paintings stolen from prominent Jewish collectors, including masterworks by Van Gogh, Cezanne and Jan Steen, until they could be picked by a middleman working for agents of Hitler's henchman Hermann Goering.

The WJC also released documents from the Secretary of State to the U.S. Embassy in Berne alleging that the Union Bank was second only to Credit Suisse in violating the Allied "Code of Conduct" in dealing with the Axis powers.
The 1945 documents also said that the Union Bank violated "the less rigid regulations" which the Swiss banking industry put into effect in September 1944.
The documents cited a two-week period of intercepts as showing that the Union Bank "provided the enemy" with 603,205 Swiss Francs (about $150,000 at the time).
